content:
Rumour has it that Apple's iPhone lineup this fall will centre around the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra. Here are the three most important feature differences—not including price—that could influence your decision to upgrade.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but it's worth mentioning because it's also the most important.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will adopt the basic design language that iPhones have used for years. Word is their screen sizes and overall design will be identical to the previous generation. If you want that classic iPhone feel, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your go-to choice.

Meanwhile, the iPhone Ultra will be Apple's first-ever foldable model. It sports a completely different form factor, with an outer screen that's shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner display resembles an iPad mini.

Camera: Pro Models Still Reign Supreme

Apple has always poured its most cutting-edge, creative camera tech into its Pro lineup. This year is no exception.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to offer many of the same camera features as the iPhone 18 Pro, but with one major exception: it won't have a telephoto lens.

Rumours suggest the iPhone Ultra will still pack the same main lens, ultrawide lens and front-facing camera as the Pro models. But the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro lineup, and is expected to perform even better this year.

Performance: Both Pack the A20 Pro Chip, but the Materials Differ

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are both expected to run on the A20 Pro chip. However, performance may vary due to differences in design and materials.

The iPhone 18 Pro will carry over the same all-aluminium unibody design from the iPhone 17 Pro, and will likewise feature a vapour chamber cooling system. These two changes made the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance superior to its predecessor, as the iPhone can maintain lower temperatures when running demanding tasks.

Meanwhile, the iPhone Ultra will adopt a streamlined titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapour chamber, though so far only one tipster has mentioned this. However, owing to the different materials, even with the same chip as the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Ultra may perform slightly worse under the blazing sun or when tackling intensive tasks.
